before_times: How many horses, their ages, and about how much each weighs
Has any horse ever kicked, bitten or struck at a person? (a yes sends the request to the owner first)
Shod or barefoot now, and what's needed: a trim, new shoes, a reset, or something corrective
How long since the last visit, and any lameness or a crack the owner knows about
The barn: a private barn, a boarding stable or a field, and a covered, level, dry place to work
after_time: Who holds the horse, and does the horse stand well?
Will the horse be caught and clean, in the cross-ties or a stall?
Water and shade nearby, and where the truck can park
A vet's order for shoes or pads, if there is one
Other horses or dogs near the work area
secure_page_only: The gate or barn code, and where a key is kept
The vet's name and phone, an emergency contact, and the vet-care OK with a spending limit
The vet's written plan for corrective or therapeutic shoeing
The horse's health conditions and medicines
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older) who owns the horse or leases it with the owner's OK. A barn manager books for a boarder only with the owner's OK. Nobody under 18 books, and a teen holds a horse only with an adult at the barn.

stop: a horse that is hurt, bleeding badly, down, in colic pain or can't put weight on a leg, right now
a person kicked, stepped on or bitten and hurt
a horse loose on a road or lost right now
a horse with hot, painful hooves that won't walk
a horse that can't be held safely
safety_and_stop_words.go_on: No, for an emergency now or for hot, painful hooves. Yes, after the owner's OK, for a horse that has kicked or bitten. Yes with a handler or a vet's sedation, for a horse that can't be held.
stop_action: A horse hurt, down, in colic pain or unable to bear weight now: Rosie can't judge how sick a horse is. It says to call the vet, or an emergency equine vet, now. No booking until the horse is safe.
A horse loose now: Rosie gives the business's number to call, and tells the owner at once.
Hot, painful hooves that won't walk: no trimming or shoeing until a vet has seen the horse. The vet's written plan then goes on the secure page.
A horse that can't be held safely: no work until a handler is there or a vet has sedated it. The farrier can stop at any time.

prep: Catch and clean the horse, and bring it to the work area
Have a handler there to hold the horse
Keep other horses and dogs away from the work area
Put the gate code on the secure page, never in a text

skills: Corrective and therapeutic shoeing (lead farrier only)
Hot shoeing and custom shoes at the forge
staff.licenses_or_certificates: None per person unless the state's form says so. A certification is the farrier's own word.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs a horse with a kicking history, every fee, every refund and every corrective shoeing price. The office manager may OK prices over the limit; the owner's answer wins.
staff.ratio: One farrier at each horse. An apprentice works only while the lead farrier is on the job.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older) who owns the horse or leases it with the owner's OK. A barn manager books for a boarder only with the owner's OK. Nobody under 18 books, and a teen holds a horse only with an adult at the barn.
children_and_age.minors_texts: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at the barn isn't the booking's adult.

visit.check_in: At the barn: the owner or handler gives the check-in code to the farrier at the work area. At the shop: the code is given at the shoeing bay. DONE with a photo of the finished hooves confirms the visit.
visit.done: DONE with the work done and a photo of the finished hooves.
visit.changes_at_visit: Pads, a wall repair or an extra horse only when the customer says yes first, priced from the list. It is paid with the visit.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Usually none: most places license neither farriers nor horse shoeing. A farrier may hold a voluntary certification, which shows only as the business's own word. A city or county may ask for a business license. The state's or city's form says which.
license.who: The business. A certification, where a farrier has one, is that farrier's own word.
license.ask: The business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one.
license.insurance: Liability insurance that covers horses in the farrier's care is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.

never_in_a_text: A horse's health conditions, medicines and vet records
